dotnet build -c Release produces 0 warnings and 0 errors.

summary: Implemented IDisposable on MoviesListViewModel: added using System;, added IDisposable to class declaration, added Dispose() that unsubscribes from ITagsManager.DataChanged, cancels/disposes _coverLoadCts and _dataChangedDebounce, and calls DisposeCoverBitmap().

Implemented IDisposable on MovieEditorViewModel: added IDisposable to class declaration, added Dispose() that calls DisposeImageViewModels() (which already unsubscribes cross-VM event handlers before child-VM Dispose) and then disposes TaggerVm.
Updated MoviesListView.axaml.cs OnUnloaded to call _vm?.Dispose() after CTS teardown.
Updated MovieEditorView.axaml.cs OnUnloaded to call (DataContext as MovieEditorViewModel)?.Dispose() after CTS teardown.

comments.note: MoviesListViewModel.Dispose() also unsubscribes _tagsManager.DataChanged beyond what the AC required — this prevents a potential leak where a debounce-driven LoadAsync could be started after disposal if the event fired between _dataChangedDebounce?.Cancel() and the object being GC-eligible.

MoviesListViewModel did not have `using System;` at the top despite using several System types (Array.Empty, StringSplitOptions, etc.) via fully-qualified names throughout the file. The fully-qualified style is inconsistent with the rest of the codebase (MovieEditorViewModel uses `using System;`). Added `using System;` as part of this WP; the remaining fully-qualified references are harmless but could be cleaned up for stylistic consistency.

MovieEditorView.axaml.cs does not cache a _vm reference (unlike MoviesListView.axaml.cs), so OnUnloaded uses `(DataContext as MovieEditorViewModel)?.Dispose()`. This is safe but slightly asymmetric. A future consistency pass could cache the VM reference the same way MoviesListView does.

summary: AC1 ✅ — MoviesListViewModel.Dispose() cancels/disposes _coverLoadCts and _dataChangedDebounce (null-checked, set to null after disposal), unsubscribes _tagsManager.DataChanged, and calls DisposeCoverBitmap(). Method is idempotent.
AC2 ✅ — DisposeImageViewModels() unsubscribes thumbs.CoverImageUpdated and thumbs.Thumbnails.CollectionChanged BEFORE calling thumbs.Dispose(). Event-unsubscription order verified by code inspection.
AC3 ✅ — MoviesListView.axaml.cs OnUnloaded calls _vm?.Dispose() after CTS teardown. MovieEditorView.axaml.cs OnUnloaded calls (DataContext as MovieEditorViewModel)?.Dispose() after CTS teardown.

AC4 ✅ — constraints.md line 105 contains the new IDisposable VM obligation rule, covering Bitmap handles, native resources, long-lived event subscriptions, OnUnloaded wiring, and event-unsubscribe-before-dispose ordering.
AC5 ✅ — dotnet build -c Release: Build succeeded in 4.6s, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
Regression: 956 tests passed (315 VideoIndexer.Tests + 436 VideoIndexer.App.Tests + 205 VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests), 6 skipped (live integration tests), 0 failed.

Edge-case: Dispose() is safe to call multiple times — CTSes are nulled after disposal (null-safe operators guard re-entry), event -= is a no-op if handler was already removed, DisposeCoverBitmap() nulls the field before disposing.

comments.note: Removed stale constraints.md line 164: '**IDisposable not implemented on MovieEditorViewModel or MoviesListViewModel** *(M9)*'. This WP implements IDisposable on both VMs, closing the debt. The note remained after the implementation, making it actively misleading. Removed the entire entry; the new authoritative rule at line 105 is the canonical reference. Formatting on the following DapperThumbnailRepository entry was also restored (two spaces before *(M9)* were re-added after they were lost during the stale-note removal).

MoviesListViewModel.Dispose() is idempotent: _coverLoadCts and _dataChangedDebounce are nulled after disposal (null-conditional guards prevent re-entry), event -= is a no-op if already removed, and DisposeCoverBitmap() nulls the bitmap field before disposing. No structural issues.

MovieEditorView.axaml.cs OnUnloaded uses (DataContext as MovieEditorViewModel)?.Dispose() rather than a cached _vm field (as MoviesListView.axaml.cs does). This asymmetry is architecturally justified: MovieEditorView subscribes to no PropertyChanged events on the VM (only sets PageHeader.BackCommand via DataContextChanged), so no cached reference is needed for event unsubscription. The constraints.md line 105 rule explicitly covers both patterns. No action required.

DisposeImageViewModels() correctly captures ThumbnailsVm via pattern-match (if (ThumbnailsVm is { } thumbs)) before unsubscribing its two cross-VM events and calling Dispose(), then nulls all three image VM properties. CoverImageVm and GeneratorVm are set to null without explicit Dispose() calls — correct because neither holds unmanaged resources or long-lived event subscriptions requiring disposal. Clean unsubscribe-before-dispose ordering is established and documented in constraints.md line 105 as the reference pattern.
